name: Element (Matrix)
tagline: Federated, end-to-end encrypted chat on an open protocol
description: Element is the flagship client for Matrix, an open standard for decentralised communication. You run a homeserver (usually Synapse); your users can talk to people on any other Matrix server, with end-to-end encryption for private conversations.
licenseNote: Synapse and the Element apps are AGPL-3.0, with a commercial licence available. Element also sells ESS Pro, which adds proprietary components for large deployments; the community stack is complete without it.
backing: Element (New Vector Ltd, UK) builds the apps and Synapse; the non-profit Matrix.org Foundation stewards the protocol

maturity.rationale: Used at national scale in the French and German public sectors. The ecosystem is mid-way through its 'Matrix 2.0' transition (new mobile apps, new sign-in service, new calling), which makes self-hosting documentation a moving target.

selfHosting.summary: A homeserver, PostgreSQL, an authentication service, media relays for calls and DNS delegation records all have to agree with each other. Element's official community distribution packages them as Helm charts for Kubernetes; Docker and Ansible setups are community-maintained.

requirements.notes: Joining large public federated rooms raises memory and database needs sharply.

managedHosting.label: etke.cc
managedHosting.note: Independent managed Matrix hosting built on the community playbook

strengths: End-to-end encryption by default for private conversations
Federation: work with people on other organisations' servers without guest accounts
An open protocol with several independent clients and servers, so no single vendor can close it
Bridges connect rooms to Slack, Teams, IRC and others during a transition
weaknesses: The hardest of the chat options to self-host well
Threads and search are less polished than Slack's, and encryption limits server-side search
Device verification and key backup confuse non-technical users
Slack import relies on community tooling and loses more than Mattermost's or Zulip's importers

featureNotes.calls: Element Call, which needs its own media server
featureNotes.slack-import: Community migration scripts and bridges only
